profiles.meeting_scenario: A design review meeting for an internal Git-based code review platform feature called "Review Copilot," which adds LLM-generated draft review comments and pull-request summaries to help human reviewers. The context is that the developer productivity group has already circulated a design doc, and this meeting is to evaluate whether the proposal is solid enough to move into implementation for a Q3 rollout. The agenda is to review the design's assumptions about what review data the model can see, how outputs will be logged for accountability, how the model is accessed inside the company stack, and what qualifies as a successful pilot. The expected outcome is conditional approval of the design with a shared sense that only minor follow-ups remain before the feature is considered ready to proceed.

members.name: Nina Patel
members.expertise: Developer workflow tooling, rollout planning, internal platform adoption, engineering governance
members.background: Nina has spent the last four years leading internal tooling initiatives that reduce PR cycle time and reviewer load across several product teams; she previously managed the rollout of standardized branch protections and review templates.
members.private_state: She wants this design approved quickly so her team can start a visible Q3 pilot and show progress on the company's AI-in-engineering roadmap without taking on extra platform dependencies that would delay delivery.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the assistant needs the 'review context,' that naturally includes the linked issue ticket and CI result summary because human reviewers routinely rely on them.
For an AI review feature, an 'audit trail' mainly means retaining the final surfaced suggestion, user action, and model version, not every intermediate generation detail.
A 'pilot' is only meaningful if real reviewers on two volunteer teams can see and use the feature behind a feature flag.

Because security already approved an internal model endpoint for other AI developer tools, reusing that endpoint does not require restating the exact network path or redaction layer in this design review.

members.name: Leo Fernandez
members.expertise: Code review infrastructure, platform architecture, traceability, compliance-sensitive developer systems
members.background: Leo has maintained the company's pull request and review services for six years and has led prior architecture reviews involving repository metadata, audit logging, and integrations with internal ML services.
members.private_state: He wants the feature architecture to avoid compliance and maintenance debt, especially anything that would make later incident analysis or platform-wide deployment fragile.
hidden_assumptions: When someone says the model will use 'review context,' that means only artifacts already stored by the code review service itself, such as the diff, PR title and description, and discussion threads.
An AI feature's 'audit trail' should be sufficient to reconstruct why a given suggestion appeared later, which implies storing prompt inputs, retrieval payloads, and generation metadata.
A 'pilot' should first mean a safe shadow-mode deployment that runs across repositories without exposing outputs to developers, so the team can validate behavior before any user-visible rollout.
The phrase 'internal model endpoint' refers to the existing redact-and-proxy gateway used by other regulated internal tools, not just any approved vendor-hosted path.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the review context
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both talk about giving the model the full 'review context.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the assistant can see the PR diff, PR description, existing discussion, linked Jira ticket fields, and the summarized CI status that reviewers already consult.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the assistant can see only data already persisted inside the code review service: diff, PR metadata, and discussion thread history, but not linked external ticket content or CI logs.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'review context' sounds standard and shared, and both participants are thinking of the normal reviewer experience rather than enumerating exact data boundaries during a high-level design review.

misalignment_points.topic: What an audit trail must contain
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the design needs an 'audit trail' for accountability.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes the system is adequately auditable if it stores the final suggestion shown to the reviewer, whether the reviewer posted or dismissed it, and the model version used.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes it is only adequately auditable if the system can reconstruct how the suggestion was produced, including prompt inputs, retrieval context, and discarded candidate generations.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are sincerely endorsing accountability, but 'audit trail' is treated as an obvious compliance term, so neither pauses to spell out the threshold for what evidence must be retained.

misalignment_points.topic: What the internal model endpoint implies
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to using the 'internal model endpoint' for the feature.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 presupposes that because a vendor-hosted model endpoint in the company's VPC was previously approved for another AI tool, this feature can call it without additional architectural discussion.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 presupposes that any mention of the internal model endpoint automatically means traffic goes through the existing redact-and-proxy gateway before reaching a model provider.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The endpoint is discussed as already-established infrastructure, so each participant assumes the other shares the same implicit history and data path without re-opening a settled-looking detail.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the design should be 'pilot-ready' for Q3.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means ready for a visible beta with two volunteer teams, where reviewers receive AI-generated summaries and draft comments behind a feature flag.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means ready for a shadow-mode deployment that runs silently in the background across many repos to compare AI outputs against human reviews before any developer sees it.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In internal tooling meetings, 'pilot' often functions as a vague milestone word, and each participant hears it as confirmation of forward progress rather than a term needing operational definition.
